therapy_note: Bhairav is the raag of Lord Shiva at dawn — it carries the quality of the first light as it touches something ancient and sacred. The two komal notes (Re and Dha) on either side of the scale create a unique symmetry — a solemn, perfectly balanced gravity. It is serious without being heavy, devotional without being supplicatory. Singing Bhairav at sunrise fills the morning with intention, weight, and sacredness.

classical_reference: Pandit Bhimsen Joshi's Bhairav recordings and Ustad Rashid Khan's morning concerts. Bandish: 'Bhor Bhai Din Chadh Gayo Meri Ambe'. Note: Bhairav and Bhairavi are completely different raags — different notes, different times, different rasas.
notes_for_vocalist: Do not confuse Bhairav with Bhairavi — Bhairav has komal Re and komal Dha (with shuddh Ga and Ni); Bhairavi has komal Re, komal Ga, komal Dha, and komal Ni. Bhairav has a masculine, solemn quality while Bhairavi is tender. The komal Dha is the vadi — give it full weight. Morning raags should be sung slowly and with gravitas.
